partially_covered.missing: Organization details are still limited to name, address, and GLN/identifier. No modeling of VAT number, legal form, contact info, or other EN 16931/D96A organizational attributes.

ValidationConstraint class exists, but no SHACL shapes, OWL rules, or explicit individuals for D96A/EN 16931 mandatory fields. No machine-readable constraints for itemized price sum or required identifiers.

cq_coverage.details: Coverage remains strong for invoice structure, participant roles, itemization, and business process assignment. However, organizational detail and explicit file format validation are still only partially modeled. No new CQs are fully addressed since last iteration.

strengths: Rich and deep class hierarchy reflecting EDIFACT and business roles
Comprehensive use of object/data property restrictions for structural validation
Clear disjointness between key conceptual partitions
All classes and properties are annotated
weaknesses: No general class axioms (GCAs) or equivalence axioms for necessary and sufficient class definitions
Limited modeling of code lists and EDIFACT code values
No explicit modeling for temporal context or document lifecycle events

reasoner_risks: Hermit/Pellet may warn on large numbers of inverse functional properties if data is inconsistent

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Expand Organization class to include VAT number, legal form, contact information, and other mandatory EN 16931/D96A attributes via new classes and data properties.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Completes CQ5 and improves regulatory compliance.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Model SHACL or OWL-based validation constraints as individuals or rules, explicitly representing D96A/EN 16931 mandatory fields and value checks (e.g., itemized price sum, required identifiers).
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables automated validation and fully answers CQ13.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add general class axioms (GCAs) and owl:equivalentClass axioms for classes like Buyer, Seller, and InvoiceMessage to capture necessary and sufficient conditions.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Increases reasoning power and semantic precision.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Model EDIFACT code lists and segment/element codes as individuals or subclasses, linking them to segments and data elements.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enhances technical vocabulary and supports code-based queries.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add temporal properties (e.g., validFrom, validTo, issueDate as xsd:dateTime) to support queries about document lifecycle and historical context.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables temporal reasoning and richer provenance tracking.

suggestions_ignored: Expand Organization attributes to include additional mandatory details (e.g., VAT number, legal form, contact information) as per EN 16931 and D96A directory.

Add general class axioms (GCAs) and owl:equivalentClass axioms for classes like Buyer, Seller, and InvoiceMessage.

improvement_tracking.notes: No improvement on previous high-priority suggestions. CQ and quality scores remain unchanged. No new issues introduced, but major enhancement recommendations remain outstanding.

summary: The ontology remains robust and strongly models EDIFACT invoice structure, roles, and itemization, with full OWL 2 DL compliance and rich annotations. However, none of the high-priority improvement suggestions from the previous review were implemented, leaving coverage and quality scores steady but not improved. To progress, explicit modeling of organization mandatory attributes and machine-readable validation constraints is required.
